newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore PM hopes visit will boost Philippines ties.
newsitem.headline: Singapore PM hopes visit will boost Philippines ties.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong hopes to use a forthcoming visit to the Philippines to boost relations which were nearly severed in 1995 after the hanging of a Filipino maid for murder.

"There was a freeze in momentum, but that freeze was temporary...I hope with my coming visit, we should be able to restore the momentum to previous level," Goh told five visiting Filipino journalist in an interview released on Saturday.
A text of the interview held on May 30 was released by the government.
Goh is scheduled to visit the Philippines from June 9 to 11.

Goh said he was bringing a big team of business people with him in an effort to "kick the momentum forward". He has also included Australian members of the Singapore-Australian Business Alliance Forum on the trip if approved by Philippines.

"If they (Philippines government) agree, then we have a new angle because it becomes a tripartite kind of arrangement for economic cooperation, which is my purpose because I think Australia also has something to offer by way of investment in the Philippines," Goh said.
Relations between Singapore and the Philippines came close to breaking in 1995 when a Filipino maid was hanged in Singapore for the murder of a young Singapore boy in her care and a fellow maid.
Many Filipinos believe the maid, Flor Contemplacion, was innocent.
The Philippines and Singapore withdrew their envoys after the maid was executed and relations were restored only last year.
Goh said the Philippines under President Fidel Ramos has made great economic progress. "Economically, President Ramos has turned the country around."
"Within a matter of two years, your brownouts (power outages) now have become a thing of the past. So investors came in."
But Goh said crime remains a problem although it is managed.
Praising Ramos, Goh said, "I think domestically he's brought peace to the Philippines, your Muslim movement in the south, your communist insurgency, those have been brought under control."
